title: Depth at least two for a normal local domain
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian local domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] that is integrally closed in its fraction field, with $\dim A\ge2$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then $\operatorname{depth}(A)\ge2$ [def-weil-pbc-depth].

source.place: Tag 031S (lemma-criterion-normal), forward implication, second paragraph; Tag 0BHZ

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kollar-local-dichotomy] to the Noetherian local normal domain A [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. The dimension bound rules out a field, since Mathlib ringKrullDim_eq_zero_of_isField gives dimension zero. The Artinian case is therefore impossible by Mathlib IsArtinianRing.isField_of_isDomain; the regular dimension-one case contradicts the bound directly. In the extension case, choose a nonzero element x in the maximal ideal, which is nonzero because A is not a field. The equality m^n ker(phi) = 0 implies x^n a = 0 for every kernel element a; the domain property gives injectivity of phi. Convert the annihilator condition to absence of the maximal ideal from associatedPrimes, and use [lem-weil-pbc-nonzerodivisor-if-maximal-not-associated] to obtain y in m acting injectively on B. Since B is nonzero, y is nonzero. Set c=y^n, which is nonzero and acts injectively on B. The conductor hypothesis says that for every b there is a unique g(b) in A with phi(g(b))=phi(c)b. Injectivity of phi gives g(1)=c, g(b+d)=g(b)+g(d), c g(bd)=g(b)g(d), and g(phi(a))=ca. These identities construct an A-algebra map f:B -> Frac(A), f(b)=g(b)/c. Regularity of c on B makes f injective. Every b is integral over A by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]; its image under f is integral [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], so integral closedness gives f(b)=a for some a in A. Injectivity of f gives b=phi(a). Thus phi is bijective, contradicting the extension case. The remaining dichotomy case is depth at least two [def-weil-pbc-depth].
